cards.title: Qualified Alternatives to Independent Free-Fraction Back-Scaling in PTA
cards.claim: Where back-scaling total exposure with an independent fu approximation is inadequate, consider qualified direct free-concentration modeling or a justified joint/deconvolution approach using individual binding information. A total-exposure PTA analysis is a different option only when its target is independently established on a compatible total-concentration basis; merely relabeling a free target is not sufficient.
conditions: PTA uses an explicit free or total exposure index and a compatible target definition.
The dependence of total exposure and binding, extraction assumptions and analytical uncertainty are considered.
required_inputs: Total and/or directly measured free exposure with assay provenance.
Individual binding information or a justified joint distribution, including relevant covariance assumptions.
PK/PD target with free/total basis, exposure window and derivation context.
limitations: Low free concentrations can introduce analytical variability.
Deconvolution depends on distributional and mechanistic assumptions and may require numerical methods.
When the needed information is unavailable, report the approximation and sensitivity rather than claiming bias-free PTA.
cards.downstream_use: Choose an exposure representation consistent with the qualified target and retain the uncertainty of the total/free relationship.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
